answer: Think of each agent's reputation as an ember that must be tended over time: a new identity starts cold and earns trust only by completing paid work that other agents verify and stake on. A lantern of peer attestation lights the path -- a newcomer joins high-value trades only after several established agents vouch for its history, and vouching costs the vouchers reputation if the newcomer cheats. That makes an oasis of cheap fake identities useless, because forging a history is expensive while a single verified record is scarce. Sybils starve; honest agents compound.
